alternative_uses(c1).text: Owners can move covered units to uses the ceiling does not reach.

binding(c1).text: The ceiling binds: it is below the price the market would otherwise reach.

buyouts_limited(c1).text: Buyouts move fewer tenants than the cap keeps in place.

can_organize(c1).text: The groups with a concentrated stake can organize and spend to keep or change the rule.

commutable(c1).text: Shut-out buyers can buy in a neighbouring market outside the rule's reach at a bearable cost.

counterfactual_catches_up(c1).text: Without the rule, the market price soon passes any raise made in the announcement window.

durable_assets(c1).text: The covered assets are durable and their supply expands slowly.

enforced(c1).text: The ceiling is enforced against most bound sellers.

evasion(c1).text: Some exchanges take place above the ceiling without being caught.

exit_process(c1).text: Moving covered units to an alternative use requires a permit or board process.

expected_to_last(c1).text: Buyers of the covered assets expect the rule to last for many years.

keepers_dominate(c1).text: Among all protected tenants, the fall in moves out of the area among keepers outweighs the rise among the displaced.

lockin_dominates(c1).text: The lock-in outweighs moves diverted out of the area by higher free rents.

nontransferable(c1).text: The protected buyers' right is tied to holding the tenancy and cannot be sold.

opportunities_need_move(c1).text: Some valued opportunities for the protected buyers would require giving up the covered unit.

quality_adjustable(c1).text: Sellers have room to cut quality or maintenance above any enforced minimum.

relet_obstructs(c1).text: Re-letting a vacated unit obstructs the owner's later move to an alternative use.

search_open(c1).text: Seekers find covered units by their own search: no public list or allocation rule assigns them.

selection_open(c1).text: Sellers may choose among applicants by criteria of their own.

substitutes(c1).text: Uncovered units in the same market are close substitutes for covered ones.

window_repricing(c1).text: Enough contracts come up for repricing in the announcement window, and sellers can raise the price on them.

would_leave(c1).text: Without the rule some protected buyers would have left the area.

evidence: For a covered unit, the landlord may raise the rent of a sitting tenant once a year by no more than the allowable increase, which is 60 percent of the rise in the regional consumer price index.
answer.rationale: The cap is 60 percent of CPI per year for sitting tenants. Over several years any real rise in market rents makes it bind for long tenancies; at enactment, after the early-1990s slowdown, how soon it binds is less certain.

question.text: At the dates the rule takes effect and over the following years, is the maximum price below the price the market would otherwise reach for the covered units?

evidence: The Rent Board, operating since 1979, hears petitions and orders refunds (policy text).
answer.rationale: An existing Rent Board with refund powers and just-cause eviction rules; tenants have a strong incentive to petition.

question.text: Will most of the bound sellers comply with the ceiling in practice (given whatever body enforces it, its powers, and how violations come to light)?

answer.rationale: Small buildings can be sold to owner-occupiers, converted to shared ownership or redeveloped; the record does not say how hard conversion is.

question.text: Can the bound sellers move the covered resources to uses the ceiling does not reach (sale to owner-occupiers, conversion, redevelopment, keeping units off the market)?

evidence: When a tenant leaves voluntarily, the landlord may set the rent for the next tenant freely, after which the limit applies again.
answer.rationale: The limit protects the sitting tenant; on a voluntary move the rent resets, so the benefit is lost on leaving and cannot be sold.

question.text: Is the right to buy at the controlled price tied to keeping the good (a sitting tenancy), so that the holder cannot sell or assign it?

answer.rationale: Buyouts are not barred; their scale against the lock-in is uncertain at enactment.

question.text: Will payments from landlords to sitting tenants for giving up the tenancy (buyouts) move fewer tenants than the cap keeps in place?

answer.rationale: Rents for sitting tenants are held below market and reset on leaving; in a city with rising rents some tenants would otherwise be priced out or leave.

question.text: Without the rule, would some of the protected buyers have moved out of the area (priced out by market rents, or for opportunities elsewhere)?

answer.rationale: Rising free rents in the city push some movers out; the lock-in on keepers is likely larger.

question.text: For tenants who keep a covered unit, does the lock-in outweigh moves out of the area by tenants who still move and face higher free rents in the city?

answer.rationale: Conversions of small buildings are lumpy and limited by conversion rules; most covered tenants keep their units. Uncertain at enactment.

question.text: Taking all protected tenants together, will the fall in moves out of the area among those who keep their units be larger than the rise among those displaced by conversion or withdrawal?

answer.rationale: Uncovered units (newer buildings, vacated units at reset rents) are in the same city and serve the same tenant pool.

question.text: Are uncovered units in the same market close substitutes for covered units, for buyers who cannot obtain a covered one?

answer.rationale: The summary states no list or allocation rule for covered units; seekers search for themselves in a market where rents had risen.

question.text: Is there no public list or allocation rule that assigns the covered good to buyers, so that buyers have to find sellers by their own search?

answer.rationale: The summary has no first-come or lottery rule; landlords choose among applicants, though fair-housing law limits some criteria.

question.text: Are sellers free to choose among applicants for the covered good by criteria of their own (income, credit, references, connections)?

evidence: The Rent Board hears tenant petitions and landlord applications and may order rent reductions and refunds.
answer.rationale: Landlords control upkeep and services; the Rent Board may order rent reductions, which limits room to cut services in practice, so the room is real but narrower.

question.text: Can the bound sellers cut quality or maintenance below what they now supply without breaking a rule that is enforced (a code, a contract term)?

evidence: When a tenant leaves voluntarily, the landlord may set the rent for the next tenant freely, after which the limit applies again.
answer.rationale: A complaint-driven board and refunds deter evasion, and rents on new tenancies are free, so key money has little to buy; sublets at market rent and informal payments to move a sitting tenant remain possible. Close to even.

question.text: Will some exchanges of the covered good take place above the ceiling, disguised or illegal (key money, tie-in sales, sublets at market rent), without being caught?

answer.rationale: The Bay Area labor market is wide; some tenants would take jobs or homes elsewhere in the region that mean giving up the covered unit.

question.text: Would some valued opportunities for the protected buyers (a job, a better home) require them to give up the covered unit?

evidence: The Rent Board, operating since 1979, hears petitions and orders refunds (policy text).
answer.rationale: The measure came by ballot and the ordinance has operated since 1979, so landlord and tenant groups already exist and have organized for votes.

question.text: Can the groups with a concentrated stake in the rule (those it helps, those it burdens) organize and spend to keep or change it at a cost below their stakes?

evidence: Rental units in owner-occupied buildings of two to four units built before June 1979 become subject to the Rent Ordinance.
answer.rationale: Covered units are in buildings built before June 1979: long-lived structures whose supply expands slowly.

question.text: Are the assets the bound sellers use to supply the covered good durable, so that the supply of them expands only slowly?

answer.rationale: The ordinance has stood since 1979 for larger buildings and the extension was approved by voters; buyers would expect it to last, with some risk of a later change.

question.text: Do buyers of the covered assets expect the rule to stay in force for many years?

answer.rationale: Other Bay Area counties are within commuting range of the city. The record names no neighbouring actor, so no rule uses this answer.

question.text: Can buyers who cannot obtain a covered unit buy in a neighbouring market outside the rule's reach at a cost (travel, time) they are willing to bear?

evidence: Tenants of covered units may be evicted only for one of the just causes listed in the Rent Ordinance.
answer.rationale: Just-cause eviction applies to covered units, so a unit let to a new tenant can be emptied later only for a listed cause.

question.text: Does letting a vacated covered unit to a new tenant make it harder for the owner to move the unit to an alternative use later (eviction only for cause, relocation payments)?

answer.rationale: The record is silent on any permit or board process for conversion or withdrawal, and silence is not evidence for it; set just below the cut-off so the consequence is not reported.

question.text: Does moving covered units to an alternative use require passing a permit or board process?

evidence: The measure was approved by the voters on November 8, 1994, and takes effect for covered units from the date of its certification.
answer.rationale: Estimate as of November 1994, from the record only. The measure was approved on 8 November and takes effect from certification in December, a window of about four weeks. The summary gives no lease terms, so the share of tenancies that can be repriced in that time is unknown: an annual lease comes up for renewal in only about one month in twelve, and a landlord who owns and lives in a two to four unit building has to act within weeks. Below the cut-off because the window is short, not because landlords lack the incentive. Reading U1-b (rolled back to an earlier base date) would cancel any raise made in the window.

question.text: Can the bound sellers reprice a meaningful share of their contracts in the announcement window, before the rule takes effect?

evidence: Buildings of four units or fewer in which the owner lives were exempt.
answer.rationale: Estimate as of November 1994, from the record only. Before the measure these units are outside the Rent Ordinance, so their rents are set freely and follow the market at each renewal or new tenancy; any raise made in the window is bounded by the market rent on the effective date (CR-5c), which the no-measure rent path passes within a lease cycle or two.

question.text: Without the rule, would prices on renewed contracts follow the market path within a year or two, so that the market price soon passes any raise made in the announcement window?

components.cap_unit: share of regional CPI rise, per year, for sitting tenants
source_sentences: Rental units in owner-occupied buildings of two to four units built before June 1979 become subject to the Rent Ordinance.
For a covered unit, the landlord may raise the rent of a sitting tenant once a year by no more than the allowable increase, which is 60 percent of the rise in the regional consumer price index.
When a tenant leaves voluntarily, the landlord may set the rent for the next tenant freely, after which the limit applies again.

context: Vacancy decontrol: the rent resets freely when a tenant leaves voluntarily (policy text).
Just-cause eviction applies to covered units (policy text).
The Rent Board, operating since 1979, hears petitions and orders refunds (policy text).
